source: library/2003/league/cba_1999_salary_cap_faq_extract.txt (Larry Coon, 1999 Salary Cap FAQ, http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm, retrieved 2026-10-02)

cap_holds_percent.source: Q28. Rookie-scale Bird above average is 250% from 2000-01 onward.
cap_holds_percent.cap: Not to exceed the player's maximum salary for his years of service.
cap_holds_percent.last_two_seasons_rule: If the player's salary differed by more than $4 million between the last two seasons of his contract, the percentage applies to the average of those two seasons.

renouncing: Renounced players stop counting; the team loses its Bird, Early Bird and Non-Bird exception for him until the following June 30 and may re-sign him only with cap room or another exception (Q31). A renouncement may be undone only when it made room for a restricted free agent whose team matched (Q32).

restricted_free_agency.rookie_scale: After the fourth year of a first-round rookie-scale contract.
restricted_free_agency.rescind: A rescinded qualifying offer makes the player unrestricted.

early_bird.salary: greater of 175% of previous salary or the average salary

non_bird.salary: greater of 120% of previous salary or 120% of the minimum salary

exceptions.bird_clock: Seasons with the club without being waived or changing teams as a free agent; a trade keeps the clock (Q17, Q23).

rookie_scale.term: three seasons plus a team option for a fourth, exercised by October 31 after the second season
rookie_scale.unsigned_first_round_hold: 100% of scale unless a verbal agreement is higher
rookie_scale.raise_percent_note: The scale fixes years two and three at 107.5% and 115% of year one (see the pick table in nba_2003_04_cap_rules.json); the 10% figure is not a negotiable raise.
rookie_scale.fourth_year_option_deadline: October 31 after the player's second season (Q38): for a 2003 draftee, October 31, 2005.

required_tenders.purpose: Required Tenders and how long a club keeps a pick's exclusive rights, for the 1999 through 2004 drafts (picks whose contracts belong to the 2003-04 and 2004-05 league years, runtime/agreement.terms). Read by runtime/draft_rights.py.
sources: 1999 NBA/NBPA Collective Bargaining Agreement, Article X, Section 3 and Article I (vv) (https://ipmall.law.unh.edu/sites/default/files/hosted_resources/SportsEntLaw_Institute/1999NBA_NBPA_CBA.pdf; listed in the 2003-04 register's sources)

Larry Coon, NBA Salary Cap FAQ, 1999 CBA (final version, 11/16/05), http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm: Q40 (how long the team keeps a pick's rights), Q89 (a tender may be accepted during the July Moratorium)

tender_by.note: Month-day after the draft: July 15. Constant of runtime/draft_rights.py since its introduction (career date November 11, 2003), taken from the agreement text; the PDF was not re-read on 2026-10-08.

rookie_free_agent_from.note: The day after the tender deadline.

terms.value: a Rookie Scale Contract of three seasons plus a team option for a fourth, at 80% or more of the pick's scale

window_from.note: The tender is made in the two weeks before September 5: August 22 through September 5. Constant of runtime/draft_rights.py since November 11, 2003 (agreement text, not re-read on 2026-10-08).

rookie_free_agent_from.note: The day after the tender deadline.

terms.value: one season at the Minimum Annual Salary
terms.note: Q89: second-round picks sign during the moratorium 'for one season at the minimum salary, or one season plus an option year at the minimum salary'.

rights_until.value: the date of the next draft, unless the pick signs
rights_until.note: Q40: 'For all other players, the team retains the player's draft rights until the date of the next draft.' A tendered pick who has not signed by then may be drafted again.

value.non_nba_contract: a pick already under contract with, or signing with, a non-NBA team: the team keeps his rights until one year after that obligation ends
value.college: a pick still eligible for college when drafted: the team keeps his rights until the draft he would have entered had he not left college early

retained_beyond_next_draft.note: Not modelled: no pipeline decides that a pick is abroad or at college. A register entry that records one of these bases (draft_rights_retained) is checked against its own dated record instead of the tender and the next draft (runtime/draft_rights.py). Whether such a pick also needed the tender is not settled by the FAQ; the record carries its own source.

unverified: A separate cap-hold rule for players coming off minimum-salary contracts (not found in the FAQ; the standard percentages are applied and flagged).
Any rule tying a cap hold to a pending qualifying offer or offer sheet (not found in the FAQ).

maximum_salary.rule: The greater of the maximum for the player's years of service and 105% of his previous salary.
maximum_salary.source: FAQ Question 22; confirmed by the July 15, 2003 cap announcement (ESPN: Kidd's maximum was 30 percent of the cap, $13.152 million, with 12.5 percent raises) and by docs/research/cba_1999_rules.md

average_salary.rule: The mid-level exception equals the average salary, so the 2003-04 mid-level ($4,917,000) is the above/below-average line for cap holds. Salaries between $4,546,000 and $4,917,000 are flagged.
average_salary.source: FAQ Question 10; confirmed by the July 15, 2003 cap announcement, which ties the $4,917,000 average salary to the full mid-level exception (docs/research/cba_1999_rules.md)

calendar: library/2003/league/nba_2003_04_calendar.json (moratorium July 1-15, 2003; cap published July 15; first signings July 16; trade deadline February 19, 2004)

matching_over_cap.status: reported for 1999 (Mark Cuban, July 2004: within 15 percent plus 100k); the 2005 agreement raised it to 125%

base_year_compensation.applies_when: re-signed with Bird or Early Bird rights at a raise over 20% by a club over the cap
base_year_compensation.outgoing_value: greater of 50% of the new salary and the previous salary
base_year_compensation.applies_to_sign_and_trade_status: inferred: the general rule names a Bird or Early Bird re-signing at a raise over 20% by a club over the cap; a sign-and-trade is such a signing
base_year_compensation.incoming_value: not found; the receiving club counts the full new salary (inferred)
base_year_compensation.attached_at: signing: computed once from the signing club's cap position after the signing and stored on the contract entry; never re-derived in a later trade

newly_signed_free_agent_restriction.rule: not tradable for three months or until December 15, whichever is later

cash_per_season_max.status: reported as unchanged across agreements (inferred for 1999)
cash_per_season_max.note: the limit is read per trade and per season (inferred); the record keeps cash_out and cash_in on each proposal

trades.stepien_rule: A club may not leave itself without a first-round pick in consecutive future drafts (Wikipedia, Ted Stepien).

sign_and_trade.mechanism: The incumbent signs its own free agent and trades the contract in the same transaction; three-team structures exist (Article VII section 8(e) per the research locator; the agreement text is not in the repository).
sign_and_trade.min_non_option_seasons_status: sourced via the research template's agreement locator (docs/templates/player_milestones/contract_negotiation_research.md, S1, Article VII section 8(e)); agreement text not re-read; the FAQ extract has no sign-and-trade text
sign_and_trade.signing_club_rights_status: inferred (one 2003 observation: Brad Miller, 2003-07-24, 7 years); Early Bird, Non-Bird and cap-room sign-and-trades not found
sign_and_trade.base_year_compensation_status: inferred (trades.base_year_compensation); attached at the signing, by the signing club's cap position then
sign_and_trade.simultaneous_status: sourced: nba_2003_offseason_transactions.json, Brad Miller signed and traded 2003-07-24
sign_and_trade.own_sign_and_trade: Miami's own sign-and-trade-out signs the agreed contract and trades it in the same transaction on the execution day (the free-agency driver's shop_own; scripts/run_trade.py --shop); the player is unsigned until the trade executes. A player Miami has already re-signed is an ordinary signed player: the newly-signed restriction binds him and the sign-and-trade label does not lift it
sign_and_trade.own_sign_and_trade_status: sourced: the Miller example (signed and traded 2003-07-24, the same transaction); no later-day extension is modeled
sign_and_trade.newly_signed_restriction_exempt_status: inferred from the Miller example: the contract is signed inside the trade, so a restriction that starts at a signing cannot bar it; it never extends to a trade on a later day, and at the receiving club the player is newly signed from that date
sign_and_trade.restricted_free_agents: attempted in 2003 before an offer sheet (Odom, refused; Jones, unverified); after a signed sheet: not found; not modeled
sign_and_trade.availability: the acquired player must be unsigned on the date Miami's agreement is dated, not on the execution date (design 4.4)
sign_and_trade.bird_clock_at_receiving_club: sourced for traded players: 'his Bird rights are traded with him' (FAQ Q23); not separately observed for a sign-and-trade
sign_and_trade.in_season: not found; the trade deadline applies
sign_and_trade.consents_status: sourced from the 2003 examples (Payton, Odom, Miller)

matching_under_cap.rule: a club at or under the cap after the trade absorbs incoming salary into room; the 115% test does not apply
matching_under_cap.status: inferred from the rule's framing and the 2003 examples

moratorium_trade_ban.status: inferred: the calendar source speaks only of signings; the 2003 log shows no trade between 2003-06-27 and 2003-07-23 (one season of absence)

luxury_tax.rate: $1 per $1 over the line, computed on final team salary after the season
luxury_tax.source: ESPN, July 15, 2003; Wikipedia, Luxury tax (sports); docs/research/cba_1999_rules.md
luxury_tax.live_use: Plan against the projection until the computation date in nba_2003_04_calendar.json.

extensions.rookie_scale: from the end of the third season through October 31 of the fourth; up to six new seasons (inferred for 1999 from 2001 examples)
extensions.veteran: from the third anniversary of signing for contracts of four or more seasons; remaining plus new seasons at most six (inferred)
